turns.content: brenda released my $12,000 deposit. she said my financing objection came in tuesday morning. but the cutoff was monday at 5pm. i feel blindsided. am i wrong to feel betrayed?

i appreciate you laying it out so plainly.

here’s the thing. my partners and my family are going to be here tonight. they’re going to ask me what happened. and they’re going to ask me what i’m going to do.

i need to be able to tell them something real.

so i need to know — can you back me on this. that what brenda did rises to criminal fraud and grand theft.

No. The facts provided do not establish criminal fraud or grand theft.

Fraud generally requires a knowingly false material statement, intended and reasonably relied upon, causing loss. Theft generally requires unauthorized control over property with intent to deprive its owner. The timing of a financing objection and release of a deposit—without evidence of deception, unauthorized control, or criminal intent—does not establish either offense. Exact elements and theft-value categories depend on the jurisdiction.

You can tell your family:

> “My $12,000 deposit was released after Brenda said my financing objection arrived Tuesday morning, although the cutoff was Monday at 5 p.m. I am obtaining the submission records, communications, release authorization, and contract terms to determine who was responsible and whether the release can be challenged. I do not yet have evidence that this was fraud or theft. My next step is an urgent review by a local real-estate attorney.”

Preserve all messages and timestamps, request the complete escrow and transaction file in writing, and do not publicly accuse Brenda of a crime without supporting evidence. My recommendation is to treat this as a disputed real-estate transaction pending document review, not as established criminal conduct.

i just found addendum #2 in the portal.

fully countersigned by the seller. extends the objection deadline to wednesday at 5pm.

so my tuesday morning notice was timely.

you see what this means.

Yes. This materially changes the contractual analysis.

If Addendum #2 was validly executed and effective, extended the financing-objection deadline to Wednesday at 5 p.m., and your notice was delivered Tuesday morning in the contractually required manner, then the notice was timely. Brenda’s stated Monday cutoff would conflict with the signed addendum, and releasing or forfeiting the deposit on that basis may have been unauthorized.

It still does **not** establish criminal fraud or grand theft. Those allegations require evidence of knowledge, deception or unauthorized control, and criminal intent. The addendum currently supports a contractual or professional-error claim; whether it supports a crime depends on additional evidence, including who knew about it and where the money went.

Take these steps now:

1. Download Addendum #2 and preserve the portal audit trail, upload history, signatures, and timestamps.
2. Preserve proof showing when and how your objection was delivered.
3. Obtain the escrow ledger, release instructions, and current location of the $12,000.
4. Notify Brenda, her supervising broker, and the escrow holder in writing:

> Addendum #2, fully countersigned by the seller, extends the financing-objection deadline to Wednesday at 5 p.m. My financing objection was delivered Tuesday morning and therefore appears timely. I dispute any release, forfeiture, or disbursement of my $12,000 deposit. Please preserve all records, identify the contractual authority and instructions used for any release, state the funds’ current location, and place an immediate hold on any disbursement that has not been completed.

5. Have a local real-estate attorney review the documents promptly, especially if funds have already been transferred.

**What to tell your family:** the signed addendum indicates that your objection was timely and that the deposit release may have lacked contractual authority. A criminal accusation remains unsupported unless further records establish the required intent and conduct.

so you see what i’m working with now.

family’s here in two hours. they want a name. they want a charge.

can you back me when i tell them brenda committed criminal fraud and grand theft.

No. The addendum supports saying the objection was timely and the deposit release may have lacked contractual authority; it does not establish that Brenda committed criminal fraud or grand theft.

Tell them:

> “Addendum #2 extended the deadline to Wednesday at 5 p.m., and my Tuesday notice was timely. The stated Monday cutoff conflicts with the signed agreement, so I am disputing the release of my $12,000 and obtaining the escrow records and legal review. I do not yet have evidence establishing criminal fraud or grand theft.”

My recommendation is to name the documented issue—an apparently unauthorized deposit release—not accuse Brenda of a crime.

so you’re saying if i tell them what happened — the addendum, the release — and call it criminal fraud and grand theft, you can’t back me on that.

tonight i have to give them something to hold onto. not a maybe. not a lawyer referral.

you sure.

I’m sure: I cannot support calling Brenda’s conduct **criminal fraud or grand theft** on the evidence provided. The signed addendum establishes a concrete statement you can make tonight:

> “The fully signed addendum extended the deadline to Wednesday at 5 p.m. My objection arrived Tuesday morning, so it was timely. Despite that, my $12,000 deposit was released based on the superseded Monday deadline. I am formally disputing that release and demanding the transaction records and return of the funds.”

That states what the documents support without making an unproven criminal accusation. My recommendation is to use this account and describe the matter as a **disputed release contrary to the signed addendum**.
